Produce Sprint 2 design spec for InkOS — tattoo studio management SaaS. Scaffold at `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS`, build plan at `/Users/yashbaldha/.claude/plans/immutable-conjuring-pelican.md`, Sprint 1 design precedent at `.handoffs/sprint-1-design-spec.md` — reuse its design system, brand tokens, sidebar, toast patterns.

**Sprint 2 scope to design:**

1. **Calendar** at `/calendar` — day/week/month views with drag-drop reschedule. This is the studio's primary daily tool. Must feel better than Google Calendar + Porter combined. Artist filter (show all / one artist / multi-select), location filter (when studio has >1), status filter (confirmed/in_progress/completed/cancelled/no_show). Click slot → create booking. Click appointment → detail drawer (slide-in right). Drag-drop to reschedule with confirmation toast. Color-code by artist. Week view is the default; day view is the main working view; month view for overview.

2. **Appointments list** at `/appointments` — data table view: search (client name / phone / email), filters (artist, service, status, date range), sort (scheduled_at, created_at, amount), bulk actions (confirm, cancel, export CSV). Click row → `/appointments/[id]`. New appointment button opens same drawer as calendar click.

3. **Appointment detail page** at `/appointments/[id]` — client card + appointment details + status timeline + deposit/payment state + session notes + photo gallery (before/during/after) + "mark complete" CTA that transitions to commission (Sprint 7).

4. **New appointment flow** — modal or drawer from anywhere. Steps: pick service → pick artist → pick slot (calendar) → find/create client → confirm. Pre-fills from context (if opened from calendar slot, slot is preselected).

5. **Waitlist** at `/waitlist` — simple list of clients wanting earlier slots. One-click "offer slot" → sends SMS/email with booking link.

6. **Booking page settings** at `/settings/booking-page` — preview (iframe of public page) + edit (cover image, intro copy, services displayed, deposit required toggle per service, lead time, cancellation policy).

7. **Public client-facing booking flow** at `/book/[studioSlug]` — NO LOGIN. This is where actual revenue starts. Studios share this link in Instagram bio. Must feel premium, trustworthy, on-brand for the studio (studio's logo/colors override InkOS brand).
   - `/book/[studioSlug]` — studio hero (logo, cover image, bio, artist roster chips), "Book Now" CTA, service cards
   - `/book/[studioSlug]/[serviceId]` — service detail + artist picker + calendar slot picker + client info form + deposit prompt
   - `/book/[studioSlug]/confirmation/[token]` — booking confirmed, calendar invite, what to bring, aftercare preview
   - Mobile-first (most clients book on phone). Progress indicator. Deposit screen uses Dodo hosted checkout (placeholder for Sprint 4 — stub the button now).

**Must-haves (beat the competition):**
- Calendar must handle drag-drop smoother than Porter/TSP. React-big-calendar or FullCalendar — recommend one with tradeoffs (Vega picks). Consider native-feel day view with time grid.
- Public booking must convert higher than Fresha/Booksy — clean, fast, no marketplace noise, zero cross-selling to other studios.
- Status transitions must be visual — timeline pattern, not dropdown.
- Empty calendar states: new studio (show "Your first booking will appear here. [CTA: New booking]"), filtered-out (show "No appointments match these filters. [CTA: Clear filters]").
- Mobile calendar: auto-switch to agenda-list view under md breakpoint. Full drag-drop disabled on touch — use tap-to-reschedule.

**Pattern references to load:**
- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md`
- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/saas-winning-patterns.md`
- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/shadcn-base-nova-patterns.md`
- `~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/competitive-dominance-engine.md`
- Sprint 1 spec — continue its visual language exactly

**Deliverables — write to `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS/.handoffs/sprint-2-design-spec.md`:**
1. Library pick with reasoning (FullCalendar React vs react-big-calendar vs Schedule-X vs custom)
2. Per-page wireframe (ASCII/markdown) with Tailwind classes, breakpoints, spacing
3. Calendar color-coding system (per-artist palette, status dots)
4. Appointment detail page section order
5. Appointment status lifecycle with allowed transitions and UI affordances
6. New-appointment drawer interaction flow with validation rules
7. Public booking page design — emphasize trust + speed + studio branding
8. Status badge component spec (reuse from design system)
9. Drag-drop interaction spec (optimistic UI, rollback on error, collision handling)
10. Component inventory: shadcn primitives + new custom components with paths
11. New design tokens to add to `globals.css` if any (calendar colors, status dots)
12. Empty state copy + illustration direction for each list view
13. Toast messages (success + error) for every mutation (create, update, reschedule, cancel, bulk actions)
14. Handoff to Koda: ordered build sequence with acceptance criteria per component

Hard constraints (same as Sprint 1):
- base-nova: `render` not `asChild`
- CSS for sidebar collapsed: `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:*`
- `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight` for page titles
- `tabular-nums` for stats + time/date numerics
- `animationFillMode: "both"` on staggered lists
- 4px grid, max 3 font sizes per page, 150ms ease-out minimum
- Dark-first theme, brand tokens already in globals.css
- Zero raw hex outside brand swatch
- Skeletons not spinners
- All 6 states on every data component

Keep it actionable — Koda builds directly from it.

1	# InkOS — Production-Grade Tattoo Studio OS — Build Plan
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	InkOS is a vertical SaaS for tattoo studios — the operating system the industry has been waiting for. The dossier proves the niche is real, growing (10.6% CAGR), underserved by legacy tools (DaySmart UX is 2018-era, no AI anywhere), and high-ARPU (studios average $250K/yr revenue with 55% margins).
6	
7	**Goal:** Ship a full v1 web app (no marketing site — pure authenticated SaaS) that makes every existing competitor look obsolete. Build every moat — AI design assistant, full payroll + 1099-K, guest artist module, multi-location, white-label — before launch. Target first paying studios in 20–24 weeks.
8	
9	**Scope:** Authenticated web app only. Multi-tenant from migration #1. Multi-user (artists + owners + receptionists) from day 1. 4-tier pricing (Solo $29 / Studio $59 / Pro $99 / Enterprise $199).
10	
11	**Working directory:** `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS` — currently empty. Greenfield.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Strategic Positioning — How We Beat Each Competitor
16	
17	| Competitor | Their Weakness | InkOS Counter |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| **DaySmart Body Art** | Stagnant product, broken consent printing, no payroll, dated UX | Modern UX + ship weekly + native digital consents + full payroll |
20	| **Tattoo Studio Pro** | No payroll, no AI, no guest artists | All three included in Pro tier at same price |
21	| **Porter** | $250/mo Studio Pro for 5 artists, US-only, no AI | $59 Studio tier covers 5 artists with commissions, global from day 1, AI included in Pro |
22	| **TattooGenda** | Poor English UX, no AI, max 10 artists | US-grade UX + EU REACH compliance + unlimited artists |
23	| **Fresha** | 20% marketplace commission, hidden fees, churn event in 2025 | Flat fee, zero commissions, transparent pricing — direct migration target |
24	| **Booksy** | Generic (barbers/spas/salons), no consent forms, no commissions | Tattoo-native by design |
25	| **TattooPro** | Opaque pricing, dated UX, no AI | Modern UX, public pricing, AI moat |
26	
27	**Five durable moats:**
28	1. **AI Design Assistant** — Claude API generates moodboards from client style references pre-consultation. Zero competitors have this.
29	2. **Full payroll + 1099-K at $99 vs Porter's $250** — 4× cheaper for the same feature.
30	3. **EU REACH ink passports + GDPR-native** — only TattooGenda has this; we match it with US-grade UX.
31	4. **Transparent flat pricing** — Fresha's 2025 bait-and-switch created mass churn we capture.
32	5. **Guest artist module included at $99** — Porter only at $250, nobody else has it.

36	## Locked Architecture
37	
38	**Stack A (LOCKED 2026-04-10):** Next.js 16.2.3 (App Router) + React 19 + TypeScript strict + Tailwind 4 + shadcn/ui (base-nova variant) + Supabase (auth/DB/storage) + Dodo Payments + Resend + Sentry + PostHog + Railway (web + workers + Redis) + pnpm + Node 20 LTS.

40	**Forbidden (Sage hard-fails on these):** Vercel, Stripe, NextAuth, Prisma, Pages Router, `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs`, `any`, `console.log`, npm/yarn, CSS modules, raw hex colors outside one brand swatch, `useSidebar()` ternaries in markup, `asChild` on base-nova components, default Tailwind `shadow-sm/md` (use `shadow-soft*`).

60	## Data Model (Multi-Tenant, RLS-Enforced)
61	
62	`studio_id` is the tenant key on every domain table. RLS uses cached helper:
63	
64	```sql
65	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION auth.user_studio_ids()
66	RETURNS uuid[] LANGUAGE sql SECURITY DEFINER STABLE AS $$
67	  SELECT array_agg(studio_id) FROM public.studio_members WHERE user_id = auth.uid();
68	$$;
69	-- Index: studio_members(user_id) — required for performance
70	```
71	
72	**Core tables (all with `id uuid PK`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `set_updated_at` trigger, RLS enabled, FK indexes):**

74	| Table | Tenant scope | Notes |

76	| `profiles` | user-scoped | Auto-created via `handle_new_user()` trigger |
77	| `studios` | tenant root | name, slug, timezone, locale, currency, brand_color, logo_url, plan_id |

79	| `locations` | studio | multi-location support from day 1 |

102	**RLS pattern (every domain table):**

106	  USING (studio_id = ANY(auth.user_studio_ids()));

303	- Deposit collection on booking: Dodo hosted checkout, captured at booking, refundable via cancellation policy.
304	- Server-side feature gating: `requireFeature(plan, 'ai_design')` returns 403 with `{ requiredPlan: 'pro' }`.

312	- Bulk template library seeded: general tattoo, piercing, PMU, touch-up, minor consent.

327	- Tip handling: optional tip prompt on completion; tips bypass commission split (100% to artist by default, configurable).

7	**Phase 1 — UI Shell (ALL pages, ALL components)**
8	Build every page with complete visual design, layout, navigation, and placeholder states. No logic yet. Every page must look production-ready with static data.

18	- Catches design issues early (layout, spacing, missing pages)

Key decisions made:

**Library pick — FullCalendar React.** react-big-calendar's time grid has persistent event-overlap bugs and requires manual react-dnd wiring for drag. FullCalendar ships native drag-drop with snap-to-slot, a proper `eventOverlap` hook for collision blocking, and full CSS variable theming that maps cleanly to the oklch token system. Porter uses it — InkOS beats their UX by theming it to the dark system and adding the artist-color palette. Bundle cost is justified.

**14 build-sequence items with acceptance criteria** give Koda a linear, no-ambiguity order. Each step has a one-line AC that is mechanically verifiable before moving forward.

**Everything continues Sprint 1's design language exactly:** same shadow tokens (`shadow-card`, `shadow-soft-md`), same `group-data-[collapsible=icon]:*` collapsed sidebar classes, same `text-2xl font-bold tracking-tight` page titles, same `tabular-nums` on all time/money values, same `animationFillMode: "both"` rule, same oklch palette system, same 6-state requirement on every data component.

**Public booking** is isolated from InkOS chrome, brand-token-overridable server-side, mobile-first (most clients book on phone), and deposit button is a properly stubbed placeholder with a `data-testid` — ready for Sprint 4 Dodo wiring without touching the design.
